section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that a person's evil inclination specifically overcomes him during divine service, and that the acceptance of these distracting thoughts stems from the aspect of falsehood within man, which is the root of the world's falsehood.
section.t: And the maamar continues,
that a person's evil inclination overcomes him to disturb and confuse him specifically during the time of divine service.
And as is seen empirically,
that specifically during the time of service of Torah and prayer, or the performance of some mitzvah,
then it seems to him,
that specifically at this moment he needs to do some matter that is most relevant to him.
For these thoughts of the Nefesh HaBahamis are intended to confuse the Nefesh HaElokis.
And the proof,
that at other times such thoughts do not occur to him.
And based on what was explained above
(section 7 and section 10)
that the matters within man
(explained in chapter twenty)
are the root of these matters in the world
(explained in the previous chapters),
it can be said,
that this [fact] that these thoughts are accepted by the person,
that although he sees that these thoughts occur specifically during the time of service
[from which he should understand even from the intellect of the animal soul that these thoughts are only to confuse him from Torah and service]
and nevertheless the thoughts are accepted by him,
is the matter of falsehood within man,
from which the falsehood of the world is derived,
that the world shows itself as a reality
(explained in the previous chapters).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains, based on the Rebbe Maharash's discourse "Mayim Rabim," that a person himself causes his own troubles and distracting thoughts about livelihood, and that if he properly contemplated that "the blessing of Hashem enriches," these thoughts would not disturb him.
section.t: And behold, it is known what the Admore"h Maharash said in the continuation of "Mayim Rabim"
at its beginning,
on the verse108
"The foolishness of man perverts his way, and his heart frets against Hashem,"
that all the evils that come to a person,
he himself caused them.
And like a person who endangers himself for luxuries,
that when an accident happens to him,
he himself caused it,
since he could have sufficed with bread to eat and a garment to wear.
And furthermore,
that even if he desires wealth,
if he had known
(and this was within his capacity)
that "the blessing of Hashem enriches"109,
and that which is also required [to act] in a natural way, as it says110
"And Hashem your G-d will bless you in all that you do," is only because the Holy One, blessed be He, desired that the blessing
(from above)
be drawn down through garments of nature,
then his activity would have been only in the manner of "the labor of your hands"111,
the toil of the hands and other external limbs, and not the toil of the brain and heart112,
and certainly he would not have endangered himself for it.
And one can connect this with what is explained in the aforementioned continuation at its beginning113
that "many waters" are the troubles of livelihood and the thoughts about worldly matters,
that this [matter] that "the foolishness of man perverts his way etc." because the evils that come to a person, he himself caused them,
also applies to the aforementioned "many waters."
For this [fact] that thoughts about matters of livelihood disturb him,
to the extent that because of this he cannot engage in Torah and service,
he himself caused it.
For if he had contemplated properly that "the blessing of Hashem enriches,"
thoughts about matters of livelihood would not have disturbed him.
And likewise regarding all the thoughts that disturb a person and confuse him from Torah and service,
that in most of them,
it is because the person brought himself to this.
And this means that from the aspect of the concealment and hiding of the world,
including also the concealment and hiding of the body and of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
as it is in itself,
even after the descent of the sin of the Tree of Knowledge and also in the time of exile,
it would not conceal and hide so much,
and the main concealment and hiding is because the person himself caused it.
And from this it is understood all the more so regarding the aforementioned thoughts
(section 14)
that occur to a person during Torah and prayer,
that if he would calculate that their occurring specifically during the time of service is because their entire purpose is to confuse him from Torah and service,
then,
not only would such thoughts not be accepted by him, but they would not even occur to him in the first place.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that even when a person has brought himself to a difficult state, the work of prayer gives him the strength to overcome, though this service itself requires great effort, both in detailed contemplation and in preparatory removal of distractions.
section.t: And behold, even when a person has brought himself to such a state,
that then the service for him is even more difficult,
nevertheless, through the service of prayer he has the capacity to overcome.
And since all matters are measure for measure,
behold, also the service of prayer itself comes through great and immense toil.
Both regarding the contemplation within prayer itself,
which is great toil, as explained in Tanya114,
and particularly that the contemplation must specifically be detailed contemplation,
due to which the service will be even more burdensome for him,
as the Admore"h
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory explains in Kuntres HaAvodah115.
And also regarding the preparation before prayer,
as the Admore"h
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory explains in Kuntres HaTefillah116,
that before prayer one must toil to remove from his mind any disturbance so that it will not disturb and confuse him during prayer.
And he explains there,
that even those who think they cannot remove the disturbances from their heart,
behold, if they would set their hearts that when they go to sleep they remove the disturbances and worries,
and if for the sake of a physical matter necessary for the body they have the ability to remove the disturbances,
all the more so that they have the ability to accomplish this in a matter pertaining to their soul.
